subject: Request: contract remedies beyond credits — termination & funds at risk
messages:
From: Mike Jensen <mike.jensen@clearline.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Clémence Dupont <clemence.dupont@clearline.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Contract remedies beyond credits — termination & funds at risk

Hi Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week — product looked solid and latency numbers were promising. Before we move to procurement, legal has flagged that credits alone aren’t sufficient for our regulatory posture. Specifically Clearline needs:

- The ability to terminate for repeated severe outages (P1) with a meaningful buyout;
- A financial mechanism beyond monthly credits — we proposed holding 3 months of committed fees in escrow as a performance reserve that can be drawn in the event of material SLA failures;
- Clear measurement windows and audit rights.

Can Redwood accept termination rights after a defined number of P1 incidents or a threshold of cumulative downtime? If not escrow, we’d accept a formal liquidated damages construct with a capped payment.

I’ve attached our draft SLA appendix and the questionnaire your security team asked for. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through specifics.

Best,
Mike Jensen
Head of Infrastructure Programs
Clearline Health

Subject: Re: Contract remedies beyond credits — termination & funds at risk

Hi Mike — thanks for the note and the attachments. Glad the demo was useful.

Short answer: we understand the ask and want to be reasonable. Credits alone are often insufficient for larger procurement teams, so we can propose a compromise that preserves our operational model while giving Clearline stronger economic protections. High level proposal we can put in the SOW/SLA appendix:

1) Safeguard Fund (preferred): Clearline deposits an agreed sum equal to 2 months of committed fees into an independent escrow/trust. Funds are not Redwood’s revenue; in the event of qualifying SLA breaches (severity P1s or cumulative downtime above a threshold) Redwood pays remediation out of that fund per a defined waterfall. Any unused funds are returned at the end of the term.

2) Termination trigger (mutual & measured): unilateral termination for cause only after either
   - 3 P1 incidents in a 90-day rolling window, OR
   - cumulative unplanned downtime > 6% for any 30-day month and >4% for a subsequent 30-day month (i.e., repeated severe degradation).
   - Before termination, Redwood will have a 30-day cure window and a single operational remediation plan/canary adjustment (we’ll cover reasonable costs of mitigation).

3) Cap and audit: total financial exposure (fund + any liquidated damages) capped at 6 months of committed fees. Clearline will have the right to audit post-incident measurement logs via a mutual NDA and agreed process.

I’ve attached a clean copy of an SLA appendix with the above skeleton for redline. Rafael is copied for legal mechanics (escrow trustee language, mutuality, measurement definitions). If this looks directionally right we can run the exact language by you and your counsel and prepare a DocuSign.

Would you be available for a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow afternoon?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLAAppendix_Clean.pdf (pdf, 92KB)]

From: Mike Jensen <mike.jensen@clearline.com>

Date: Wed, 08 Oct 2026 08:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Contract remedies beyond credits — termination & funds at risk

Laura — appreciate the quick turnaround and the pragmatic structure. A couple of asks from our side to consider before we take the draft to procurement:

- Can the safeguard fund be set to 3 months instead of 2? Our procurement benchmark is 3 months for critical platforms.
- Cure window: 30 days is fine for complex remediation, but for repeated severe outages we’d like the ability to terminate after a shorter cure for repeat offenders — e.g., if the same P1 recurrence happens within 30 days of remediation, allow a 15-day cure following the recurrence.
- Measurement: we need the definition of P1 and the measurement tooling to be explicit — who defines the start/end of an incident and whether scheduled maintenance is excluded. We’d want a joint incident postmortem for any termination-triggering sequence.

If you can accept those tweaks (or propose a middle ground), I’ll escalate to procurement/legal and we’ll aim to finalize quickly.

Thanks,
Mike

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 09 Oct 2026 11:17:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Contract remedies beyond credits — termination & funds at risk (internal)

Laura/Ben — quick legal read: overall the safeguard fund + mutual termination trigger is workable, but a few non-negotiables from our side:

1) Mutuality: termination for performance must be symmetrical — Redwood must retain the same right to cure and the same measurement constructs applied to both parties (i.e., not provider-only credit triggers).
2) Trustee mechanics: escrow should be with a neutral third-party trustee (we use "NorthTrust" in other deals). Fund disbursement must be tied to predefined thresholds and require a joint breach determination or an independent arbitrator/technical adjudicator if disputed.
3) Caps: keep the exposure capped (Rafael recommends 4 months of committed fees), but sales has proposed 6 months in your draft — we should split the difference at 5 months unless commercial insists on 6.
4) Cure windows & repeated offenses: 30-day cure window is standard; the 15-day immediate cure on recurrence is risky operationally. Counterproposal: allow a 15-day expedited remediation window only where the recurrence is reproducible and directly attributable to Redwood code/config, not to customer workloads or upgrading activity.

I can prepare redline language for the escrow agreement and the SLA measurement exhibits. If procurement insists on 3 months in the fund, we can accept 3 months but insist on the independent trustee + adjudication clause and the overall cap at 5 months.

Rafael

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Jensen <mike.jensen@clearline.com>
Cc: Clémence Dupont <clemence.dupont@clearline.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Contract remedies beyond credits — termination & funds at risk

Mike — thanks, and appreciate the thoughtful asks. We’re prepared to move to a mutual compromise to unblock procurement: final proposal below. If this is acceptable we’ll circulate DocuSign and the escrow/trustee agreement.

Final proposed terms (summary):
- Safeguard Fund: 3 months of committed fees deposited with an independent trustee (NorthTrust).
- Disbursement: funds drawn according to a three-step waterfall: (1) operational remediation credits (automatic per-incident formula), (2) reimbursement for verified customer losses tied directly to provider failure (subject to joint determination), (3) capped liquidated payment up to 5 months of committed fees.
- Termination: either party may terminate for cause after either (a) 3 P1 incidents in a 90-day rolling window, or (b) cumulative unplanned downtime >6% in a 30-day month followed by >4% in a subsequent 30-day month.
- Cure windows: standard 30-day cure following a qualifying sequence; for a repeat P1 within 30 days, an expedited 15-day remediation window will apply only where the incident is attributable to Redwood (per the joint incident adjudication process).
- Measurement & audit: P1/P2 definitions, measurement tooling, and maintenance exclusion mechanics included in SLA exhibit; mutual postmortems required for termination-triggering sequences and limited auditor access to relevant logs under NDA.

I’ll attach the DocuSign draft and the trustee agreement for review (links below). If your counsel signs off I can route for signature today.

DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/CL-2026-0921
SLA appendix (redline ready): https://drive.example.com/sla/CL-2026-0921/SLAAppendix_Clean.pdf

If that works, let’s get signatures and schedule a kickoff to align on incident measurement and the trustee onboarding.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
